research_question: In people at risk of acute kidney injury (e.g. after cardiac surgery, critical illness or trauma, contrast exposure, or kidney transplantation), do erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (epoetin alfa/beta/zeta, darbepoetin, methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta or other ESAs), compared with placebo or usual care without an ESA, reduce the incidence of acute kidney injury?
treatment_label: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (epoetin alfa/beta/zeta, darbepoetin, CERA or other ESA)
control_label: Placebo or usual care without an ESA
outcome_description: Number of participants who developed acute kidney injury (events) out of the number randomised to each arm (intention-to-treat denominator; number analysed if that is all that is reported), during the trial's follow-up. AKI defined by the trial's own definition, preferring consensus criteria in the order KDIGO, AKIN, RIFLE, otherwise the trial's stated primary definition (e.g. a defined rise in serum creatinine or fall in eGFR). Participants with AKI are counted, not episodes; need for dialysis, continuous creatinine values, or undefined "kidney dysfunction" are not accepted as AKI. Trials reporting zero AKI events in both arms are retained with arm sizes; trials not reporting AKI are excluded. In multi-arm trials only the ESA and control arms are used, with multiple ESA doses combined (events and participants summed).
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR < 1, i.e. a positive Hedges g equivalent) means fewer participants developed acute kidney injury in the ESA arm than in the placebo/usual-care arm — that is, the ESA reduced AKI incidence (favours ESA).
search_queries: erythropoietin acute kidney injury randomized controlled trial
darbepoetin epoetin renal protection cardiac surgery trial
erythropoiesis-stimulating agent contrast-induced nephropathy prevention randomized
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in adults or children, in any clinical setting, comparing an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent with placebo or usual care without an ESA (ESA given to prevent AKI or to treat another condition)
Reports the number of participants developing acute kidney injury (by any stated definition) per arm, including trials reporting zero events in both arms
Any dose, route, schedule or duration of ESA; multi-arm trials eligible if an ESA arm and a non-ESA control arm can be identified
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, narrative review, theoretical or modelling paper, conference abstract without data)

No comparison between an ESA treatment arm and a placebo/usual-care control arm (e.g. single-arm study, observational cohort without control, or control arm receiving another active kidney-protective drug)
No quantitative outcome data allowing an effect size (no AKI event counts and denominators, or only continuous creatinine/eGFR, dialysis need, or undefined 'kidney dysfunction' reported)
Completely unrelated to ESAs or to acute kidney injury outcomes
moderators_to_extract: Clinical setting (cardiac surgery, critical illness/trauma, contrast exposure, kidney transplantation, other)
AKI definition used (KDIGO, AKIN, RIFLE, creatinine threshold, eGFR fall)
Timing of administration relative to the renal insult (pre-, peri-, post-insult)
Population age group (adults vs children) and baseline kidney function
Sample size category and risk-of-bias / blinding status
effect_size_note: Pool as a random-effects risk ratio (ESA ÷ control) of participants developing AKI; RR < 1 favours ESA. Use number randomised as denominator (number analysed if only that is reported, and note it). Combine multiple ESA dose arms into a single group; retain double-zero trials visibly. Do not pool mortality, dialysis requirement, haemoglobin, transfusion, thromboembolic events or length of stay.
